previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted for worsening lower extremity edema in the setting of chronic lymphedema, morbid obesity, and recurrent cellulitis. She presented with increased swelling up to her thighs, shortness of breath on exertion, and concern for possible cellulitis in the right foot. Initial labs showed leukocytosis and normal BNP, with a clear chest X-ray, ruling out acute heart failure. She was treated with IV furosemide, adjusted for rising creatinine, and a short course of IV clindamycin for possible cellulitis, later discontinued due to lack of improvement. A transient neurologic event was evaluated by neurology and attributed to factors including volume status and sedating medications, with a normal Keppra level. Gabapentin was started for neuropathic pain, and nystatin for oral thrush. She stabilized with improved edema, continued home medications, and was discharged home with home health services and follow-up plans.

# Cellulitis: The patient presented with worsening ___ edema, 
erythema and low grade fevers concerning for cellulitis. 
Initiated on clindamycin 900mg q8h as out-patient (received 4 
doses prior to admission) and referred to ED for further 
management. She has a history of cellulitis in the past and 
bilateral worsening ___ edema making her more susceptible to 
developing an active infection. On exam, has bilateral ___ 
erythema which she says has improved with the initiation of ABX. 
Leukocytosis stable at 12.4 (has chronic elevated WBC per review 
of OMR ranging from ___. She was continued on a 10 day course 
of IV antibiotics with resolution of her cellulitis. 
 
# ___ edema/Chronic lymphedema: This was most likely secondary to 
chronic lymphedema on bumex 4mg PO daily at home for management. 
Unlikely CHF and CXR negative for significant pulmonary edema. 
From discussion with the patient it appeared that she had poor 
adherence to low salt diet. She likely gained some weight when 
her Bumex dose was decreased to every other day. Her volume was 
difficult to diurese. She consistently had I/Os that were 
documented as negative. However, there was concern she was not 
adhering to a fluid restriction. She was diuresed with 100mg 
lasix IV BID, that was then transitioned to a lasix gtt at 
10cc/hr. She was diuresed until her creatinine increased 
slightly and then switched to her Bumex daily dosing. Her weight 
unfortunately decreased only 1kg from admission to discharge.   
 
# Recurrent DVT/PE: INR supratherapeutic on admission likely in 
the setting of ABX use. On Warfarin 7mg daily as out-patient. 
Plan for daily warfarin dosing for goal INR ___. She was 
initially supratherapeutic, but by discharge she was therapeutic 
on her home coumadin dose.

# Thrush: She was initially on nystatin with minimal response so 
she was started on fluconazole with a planned seven day course.
 
# Fibromyalgia: She was continued on her very large home doses 
of narcotics with oxycodone 45 mg PO Q6H:PRN, morphine, and 
gabapentin. This has been confirmed to be her home dose in the 
past. She was frequently overly sedated on this dose and this 
should be discussed with her PCP in the future about adjustments 
given concerns about her doses and the effects on her. 
 
# Hx of seizure disorder: She was continued LeVETiracetam 1000 
mg PO BID and home Topiramate.   
 
# COPD: She was given nebs PRN with and remained stable with no 
respiratory distress. 
 
# Tobacco use: She was given a nictoine patch.
